focus_areas: Edge integrity between flipper and rock
Geometric structure of the snout and whiskers
Presence and clarity of external ear pinnae
Texture consistency of fur vs skin on flipper
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Focus heavily on the boundary between the foreground flipper and the rock. Does the shadow look physically accurate, or is there evidence of generative blending? Also, scrutinize the nose area: does the geometry hold up under close inspection, or does it appear smeared? Confirm that the visible ear flap is structurally connected to the head and not a floating artifact. Ensure the open vocabulary detector has correctly isolated the sea lion from the similar-colored rocks before assessing boundaries.
image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a sea lion resting on a rocky surface. The animal is lying on its side with its head tucked down and eyes closed. One large foreflipper is prominently visible in the foreground, draped over a rock. The fur appears short, coarse, and golden-brown, transitioning to darker shades on the head. The background consists of out-of-focus grey rocks.
